rows.notes: The document is explicitly labelled a Review Article (CJAST 2020). It summarises other studies' IoT/sensor irrigation results (e.g. water savings of 61%, 90%, 7%, 48.78% reported by cited authors) and describes a generic Arduino-based architecture and a sensor calibration procedure without reporting any own data, experiment, trial or validated results. Water-saving and labour-saving statements are secondary (Table 1 from [16], case studies from [18]-[29]). No primary evidence on IoT-enabled monitoring and water savings.

Review article; no own data. Efficiency/water-saving figures for sensor-based IoT systems are all drawn from cited studies. The system architecture (Section 3) and calibration (Section 4) are descriptive procedures, not tested results.

Review article; no own data. The study does not report any own result on resilience or risk management; it only notes in the conclusion that sensor reliability and internet connectivity limit field-level adoption, as a general opinion.

Review article; no own data. Soil-moisture-sensor water-saving results (Section 2.3, Table 4) are all reported from cited works ([18]-[29], [33], [35]-[37]); the calibration steps in Section 4 follow a published procedure and no calibration results are reported.

Review article; no own data. Nothing in the study is an own result on soil sensors delivering resilience or risk management; drawbacks of wireless sensors (battery, memory, cost) in Table 2 are generic review statements.

notes: The cited study is a narrative review (self-identified 'Review Article') of IoT-based precision irrigation. Sections 3-5 describe a generic system architecture, a sensor calibration procedure and sensor placement guidance drawn from the literature, but no experiment, measurement, survey or validated model run of the authors' own is reported. Q1 is therefore 'no' for all rows and Q2-Q9 follow as 'no'. Full text appears complete (pages 15-26 with references).
